cards.question: What is the lifetime and memory allocation behavior of a variable with the auto storage class in C?
cards.answer: Its memory is allocated on the stack when execution enters its enclosing block scope and automatically deallocated when execution leaves that scope.

cards.question: What is the default storage class for local variables declared inside a function block in C?
cards.answer: The default is auto (automatic storage duration), meaning the auto keyword is implicit and rarely written explicitly.

cards.question: When might a developer explicitly specify the auto keyword on a local variable in C?
cards.answer: When intentionally shadowing a global variable to make the local block scope and lifetime explicit in code.
